heroHeadline: ICE Deports Milo Yiannopoulos to UK as July Arrests Hit Second-Term Record of 49,571
heroSubtitle: ICE arrested British far-right commentator Milo Yiannopoulos at a New Orleans airport on Aug 27, 2026 and deported him to the United Kingdom the next day for overstaying his visa, DHS confirmed Aug 29 — a case officials used to urge other undocumented immigrants to self-deport. The deportation came as ICE arrests hit 49,571 in July, the highest single-month total of Trump's second term, up 15% from June, with Texas and Florida accounting for nearly 20,000 arrests combined. The White House separately said Aug 24 it is preparing to revoke up to 200,000 B1/B2 visas from asylum seekers, the largest mass visa revocation in U.S. history, while a two-week 'Operation Safe Community' surge across Virginia and Maryland netted 1,328 arrests and a school-year enforcement push in Danbury, CT drew condemnation from Sen. Chris Murphy over reports agents targeted parents at school bus stops. The 287(g) program has expanded to 2,179 active agreements — up from 688 when Trump took office. ICE's FY2026 detention death toll remains elevated with Acting Director Venturella's June 4 memo ending post-release death reporting still in effect, eliminating a key accountability mechanism. Combined with $45B+ in H.R. 1 and the $70B 'Secure America Act,' total 2025-2026 immigration enforcement appropriations exceed $115B — roughly 13× ICE's pre-2025 annual budget.
